question.prompt:
At a competition with \(N\) players, the number of players given elite status is equal to \[ 2^{1 + \lfloor \log_2 (N - 1) \rfloor} - N. \] Suppose that \(19\) players are given elite status. What is the sum of the two smallest possible values of \(N?\)

Note: \(\lfloor x \rfloor\) is the greatest integer less than or equal to \(x.\)

solutions.explanation:
Because \(N\) counts players and the logarithm must be defined, \(N\) is an integer with \(N\ge2\). Set
\[
m=\lfloor\log_2(N-1)\rfloor.
\]
The definition of the floor, together with the increasing powers of \(2\), gives the exact interval
\[
2^m\le N-1<2^{m+1}.
\]
The elite count is \(19\), so
\[
2^{m+1}-N=19,
\qquad N=2^{m+1}-19.
\]
Substituting into the interval checks which exponents really work:
\[
2^m\le2^{m+1}-20<2^{m+1}.
\]
The right inequality always holds. The left inequality is equivalent to \(2^m\ge20\). Since \(2^4=16\) and \(2^5=32\), this holds exactly for integers \(m\ge5\).

Conversely, every such \(m\) satisfies the floor interval, so no further candidates are lost. The value \(N=2^{m+1}-19\) increases with \(m\), making the two smallest possibilities
\[
N=64-19=45,
\qquad N=128-19=109.
\]
Their sum is \(\boxed{154}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Translate the floor into a power interval
